says: The wind now acts on the whole figure: the tunic is pressed flat against the windward side and billows on the lee side with tension folds streaming across it, the hood grows a flap that streams downwind, the skirt hem lifts and flaps to the right, and the cloth creases above and below the belt. The cloak loses its zigzag trim: long sweeping folds fan out from the shoulder to an uneven, fluttering edge, with shadow running down each trough. The ribs are in perspective now: the nearest one is huge and cropped by the frame, the rest shrink and crowd together as they recede along a half-buried spine.
